tagline.text: A walk-in marine sanctuary on Siquijor's west coast in front of Coco Grove

location.label: Location
location.text: Tubod Beach in front of Coco Grove Resort, San Juan, western Siquijor Island

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,500 (per person, entrance, gear and transport)

children.text: Tubod Marine Sanctuary is a protected reef off Tubod Beach in the town of San Juan on western Siquijor, described as one of the island's best snorkeling and diving sites. A short swim from the beach brings you to seagrass and coral reef, and the sunset here is lovely, so it fits well into a day's plan.

Tubod Marine Sanctuary lies off the west coast of Siquijor Island, in front of Tubod barangay in the town of San Juan. In the 2024 census San Juan had 17,291 residents, the fastest-growing of the island's six towns, and covers about 44.37 square kilometers. The town was formerly called Makalipay and its patron saint is St. Augustine of Hippo. It is about 12 kilometers from Siquijor town, so it is easy to reach by motorbike or tricycle. Tubod barangay has 1,203 residents, a small coastal village, but the sanctuary draws a steady stream of snorkelers and divers. San Juan ranges from sea level to 391 meters in elevation, with average daytime highs of about

and annual rainfall of about 1,047 millimeters. The town has St. Augustine of Hippo Parish Church, Paliton Beach and Capilay Spring Park, and the Bugwas Festival, the town fiesta honoring its patron saint, has been held since 2006.

According to travel write-ups, the protected reef sits right in front of the beach at Coco Grove Beach Resort. If you come by tricycle from the Lazi side, get off at the small parking area among the trees on the left just past the resort and follow the path to the sea. Sitting on the beach is reported to be free, while visitors report separate fees for snorkeling, diving and swimming. The amounts differ from source to source, so confirm on site. Because it fronts a resort, the beach is quiet and not crowded.

The underwater scenery changes in stages. Seagrass grows near the beach, and a little farther out is a reef where anemonefish live. Farther still the water deepens, and some corals grow over a meter tall. Snorkeling is allowed only in the designated area, and a floating platform at the edge makes a handy resting spot. Some write-ups say you can see sea turtles and giant clams, while others say turtles are an Apo Island thing, so go to see coral and tropical fish rather than expecting turtles.

Tubod is also a sunset spot. The beach faces west, and as the sun sets the sky turns pink and orange and reflects on the water. Some visitors say the water is very salty, so you float easily, which suits beginners. Sea urchins are plentiful, so wear water shoes. If you only have one day for snorkeling on Siquijor, pick either Tubod in the west or Tulapos in the north, whichever fits your route better.

blocks.title: Coral reef a short swim from the beach

children.text: You enter straight from the beach without a boat and reach the reef after a short swim. Write-ups describe it as one of the island's best snorkeling and diving spots. Pay the entrance fee before entering the water and stay in the designated area.
Seagrass lies close to the beach, and a little farther out begins a reef with tropical fish such as anemonefish. Farther out, some corals are said to grow more than a meter tall.
A floating platform at the edge of the snorkeling area lets you rest when you tire. The water is salty, so you float easily, and beginners are said to find it relatively comfortable.
The beach faces west, so at sunset the sky turns pink and orange. Watching the sunset from the beach after snorkeling is the standard plan here.
The sanctuary lies in front of the beach at Coco Grove Beach Resort, so guests can reach it directly. The resort is reported to rent gear, give scuba lessons and run day trips to Apo Island.

blocks.title: A spot open to divers too

children.text: One visitor report says scuba diving costs about ₱100 per diver and snorkeling about ₱50. Rates differ between write-ups, so confirm the official fee on site. Coco Grove Resort is also said to offer scuba lessons.
It is described as quiet, with few visitors. Coconut palms provide shade from the sun, and it suits families with children.

items.title: Half-day snorkeling plan
items.subtitle: A morning swim and an evening sunset

children.text: Set off by motorbike toward San Juan from your lodging in Larena port or Siquijor town. Follow the west coast road and look for Coco Grove Resort.
Past Coco Grove Resort, stop at the parking area on the left and walk to the beach. Pay the entrance fee and start snorkeling in the designated area.
Come out and rest in the shade of the palms. Reportedly there is only one restaurant on the beach and prices are high, so bring snacks.
Have lunch in San Juan town or at a nearby restaurant.
Return to the beach and watch the sunset.
If you plan to stay until sunset, factor in the trip back and riding a motorbike after dark.

You can also come from Cebu or Bohol. One write-up says ferries from Tagbilaran (Bohol) to Siquijor start at about

Sources from the 2020s say there is no regular direct flight from Manila to Siquijor. Check before you book.

You can rent a motorbike for about
a day, and there are reportedly several rental shops at the Larena terminal. Fuel is extra. A tricycle island tour is reported at about
a day for three people.
The dry season, November to May, has calm seas and good visibility on Siquijor, which suits snorkeling. Sunsets are sharper on clear days.
In the rainy season, June to October, rain and wind can raise the waves, so check the weather before deciding whether to get in the water.

If you build your plan around the sunset, you can arrive late in the afternoon and do both the swim and the sunset. Riding a motorbike after dark can be dangerous, so head straight to your lodging soon after sunset.

The only restaurant on the beach belongs to Coco Grove Resort and is reported to be pricey, so bring snacks and water. In and around San Juan, lodging ranges from budget guesthouses to mid-range and luxury resorts. Coco Grove gives direct access to the sanctuary, which is convenient. One travel blog named Miki's Guest House for budget, Tropical Fun Ta Sea for mid-range and Infinity Heights Resort for luxury. Lodging changes often, so check the latest reviews on a booking site.
Meals center on local restaurant fare such as grilled seafood and chicken dishes, and many places on the island want cash. ATM access on the island can be limited, so carry plenty of cash.
The swimming area is limited to the designated zone. Do not go outside it.
Sea urchins are plentiful, so always wear water shoes. Walking barefoot is dangerous.
Snorkeling fees and guide requirements differ between sources, so confirm the official rates on site before you go, and beware of overcharging.
The entrance hut is reported to be open daily from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. If you want to see the sunset, finish your swim early.
Bring snacks and water, and take your trash back with you.
Day trips to Apo Island are reported to require booking at Coco Grove a day ahead. If you want to combine one with your Siquijor plans, ask in advance.
Bring a waterproof bag and a power bank for your phone.

Visiting St. Augustine of Hippo Parish Church and Capilay Spring Park in San Juan shows you a side of the town you will not see from the beach alone. Check opening hours and fees locally.
Do not swim outside the designated area, and postpone entering the water when waves are high or it is raining.
Sea urchins are plentiful on the beach and in the shallows, so do not walk barefoot.
Do not step on or touch coral, and wear a rash guard because sunscreen can harm coral.
If you are not a strong swimmer, wear a life vest and stay near the platform at the edge.
Check your way back to your lodging before it gets dark at sunset.
Fees and rules can change, so follow the notice at the hut.
